items.description: Verdi's opera in a new staging by Davide Livermore, conducted by Vincenzo Milletarì (Turno C).
items.name: Il trovatore (Verdi)

items.address: Conservatorio Niccolò Piccinni, Via Cifarelli 26, 70124 Bari
items.description: Ilumina Ensemble in the 85th season of the Camerata Musicale Barese.
items.name: Classica in chiave brasiliana
items.note: Price for this concert not listed; the season's single tickets are 15-44 EUR. Box office at Via Sparano 141.

items.description: Last performance of the run of Verdi's opera staged by Davide Livermore (Turno D).
items.name: Il trovatore (Verdi)

items.description: Time Zones festival night with Danalogue's live set "Teleportations" (21:00) and System Exclusive (22:00).
items.name: Time Zones 2026: Danalogue + System Exclusive

items.description: Orchestra and Chorus of the Teatro Petruzzelli under John Axelrod in Mozart, Liszt's Piano Concerto No. 1 and Rossini's Petite Messe solennelle.
items.name: Concerto sinfonico (Axelrod)
items.note: The ticket link's slug names another pianist; the theatre's page lists Sophia Liu.

items.address: Conservatorio Niccolò Piccinni, Via Cifarelli 26, 70124 Bari
items.description: The concert hall of the Niccolò Piccinni conservatory, opened in 1981 in the grounds of Villa Lindemann.
items.name: Auditorium "Nino Rota"

items.description: A contemporary theatre run by Teatri di Bari in a former industrial shed, which also hosts concerts.
items.hours: Box office: Tue-Fri 10:30-12:30 and 16:30-19:00, and two hours before shows.
items.name: Teatro Kismet
items.note: No dates published for 24-31 October when checked.

items.description: A small brewery and art room pouring craft beer, with live indie, experimental and acoustic music and exhibitions.
items.name: Noise

items.description: A city-run creative hub in Libertà with a concert room used by festivals and club tours.
items.name: Officina degli Esordi

items.description: An independent bookshop and café-bar that hosts book launches, small concerts, theatre and debates.
items.name: Prinz Zaum

items.description: Bari's opera house on Corso Cavour, home to the city's opera, ballet and symphonic seasons and also open for short guided tours.
items.hours: Box office: Mon 10:00-14:00, Tue-Sat 11:00-19:00, Sun 10:00-13:00; opens 90 min before each show.
items.name: Teatro Petruzzelli
items.note: Guided tours listed for Sun 25 Oct 15:30 and Tue 27 Oct 13:00 and 15:30 (the page also shows a second October calendar adding Mon 26 Oct); tickets on sale 30 min before, schedule may change.
items.price: Guided tour (about 30 min): 7 EUR, reduced 2 EUR.

items.description: A rebuilt nineteenth-century market hall on Piazza del Ferrarese hosting contemporary art and design shows, talks and festival concerts.
items.name: Spazio Murat

items.address: Via Giustina Rocca, 70126 Bari (box office Via Argiro 73)
items.description: A large commercial theatre for musicals, comedy and touring concerts, with its box office in Murat.
items.name: Teatroteam
items.note: Nothing programmed for 24-31 October when checked; next show 1 November.

items.description: A manga and anime shop, opened in 2024, selling books and games imported from Japan.
items.name: Star Shop Bari Carrassi

items.description: A comic shop open since 1997 selling new and back-issue comics, gadgets and board games.
items.name: Neverland (Via Toti)

items.description: A comic shop with pre-orders and in-store events.
items.name: Kurama Shop
items.note: The site says open every day, Sunday 17:00-20:30; weekday hours are not given.

items.description: Neverland's second shop, opposite the central station at the Bari Nord exit, with the same new and back-issue comics.
items.name: Neverland (Corso Italia)

items.description: A shop for comics, manga, trading cards, video games, figures and board games.
items.name: UMI Games

items.description: The nineteenth-century grid-plan town south of Bari Vecchia, with Corso Vittorio Emanuele II, Piazza Umberto I and the shopping street Via Sparano.
items.iswcTip: The organisers recommend the lively shopping area around Via Sparano, the most characteristic street in the centre.
items.name: Murat district

items.address: Palazzo della Provincia, 4th floor; Lungomare Nazario Sauro 27 or Via Spalato 19, 70121 Bari
items.description: The city's main art gallery, from medieval and Venetian painting to Giaquinto, the Neapolitan nineteenth century and the Macchiaioli.
items.hours: Tue-Sat 09:00-19:00, Sun 09:00-13:00; free on the first Sunday of the month.
items.name: Pinacoteca Metropolitana "Corrado Giaquinto"
items.price: 8 EUR combined with Santa Scolastica, valid 2 days.

items.address: Piazza Federico II di Svevia 4, Bari
items.description: A Norman-Swabian fortress at the edge of the old town, now a state museum.
items.iswcTip: The organisers call the Norman-Swabian castle one of the symbols of Puglia; right in front of its entrance starts Arco Basso, which they call the city's most authentic alley.
items.name: Castello Normanno-Svevo
items.note: Hours and tickets are on the museum's ticketing link from the official page.

items.description: A former theatre built on piles over the sea at the old port, now a contemporary art centre.
items.name: Teatro Margherita

items.description: The south-eastern gateway to Bari Vecchia, next to Piazza Mercantile and the seafront.
items.name: Piazza del Ferrarese

items.description: The monumental seafront promenade of the 1920s and 1930s, running from Piazza Diaz past the Pinacoteca.
items.iswcTip: The organisers call it evocative and among the most beautiful seafronts in Italy, with late Liberty-style buildings, green parks and views of the Adriatic.
items.name: Lungomare Nazario Sauro

items.description: Bari's Apulian Romanesque cathedral, seat of the Archdiocese of Bari-Bitonto.
items.iswcTip: The cathedral is among the places the organisers suggest visiting in Bari.
items.name: Cattedrale di San Sabino

items.description: The old town's big historic square, once the heart of city life, with the Colonna Infame pillory column.
items.name: Piazza Mercantile

items.description: The old town's sea wall, now a walk with wide views over the Adriatic towards Santa Scolastica.
items.name: Muraglia

items.description: The Romanesque pilgrimage basilica of Bari Vecchia that keeps the relics of St Nicholas in its crypt.
items.iswcTip: One of the organisers' suggested visits in old Bari; they note that the relics of the city's patron saint, Saint Nicholas of Myra, are kept in the crypt.
items.name: Basilica di San Nicola

items.description: Bari's sandy public city beach along Lungomare Perotti, south-east of the centre.
items.name: Pane e Pomodoro beach
items.note: Swimming is often banned after heavy rain.

items.description: An archaeology museum from prehistory to the Middle Ages in a former Benedictine convent and bastion at the tip of the old town.
items.hours: Tue-Sat 09:00-19:00 (last entry 18:30); Sun and holidays 09:00-13:00 (last entry 12:30); closed Monday.
items.name: Museo Archeologico di Santa Scolastica
items.price: 5 EUR, reduced 2 EUR (18-25); 8 EUR with the Pinacoteca, valid 2 days; free under 18 and on the first Sunday of the month.

items.description: The Giannini brothers' gelateria, known for rich creams such as praline pistachio and mascarpone with pear, plus fruit sorbets and vegan, sugar-free and gluten-free options.

image.alt: A dish Il Gelatiere is known for

items.name: Il Gelatiere
items.note: The pin is the middle of the street (OSM has no point for no. 162). The shop's page writes Viale della Resistenza, 70124; OSM and ConGelato say Via, 70125. A second shop is at Viale Antonio Salandra 25.

items.description: A family-run café-bar on Via Fanelli, open since 1969, best known for its gelato topped with hand-whipped cream, with pastries and coffee too.
items.name: Bar Telebari
items.note: A café-bar rather than a gelateria, though its gelato is what it's known for. BariToday reported it reopening in early 2023 after closing over energy bills; the site lists the Via Calefati branch as temporarily closed.

items.description: An artisan gelateria in Murat, open since 2012, working with seasonal fruit and little sugar and fat, with semifreddi and gelato cakes as well as cones.

image.alt: A dish Gelateria Piccinni is known for

items.name: Gelateria Piccinni
items.note: Hours from the shop's site, which doesn't say whether they change outside summer.

items.description: A seafood restaurant on Corso Vittorio Emanuele II serving local fish and Apulian land-and-sea dishes, with outdoor tables in the warmer months.
items.name: La Muraya
items.note: The official site gives Monday as the closing day; PagineGialle says Tuesday.

items.description: Chef Antonio Scalera's restaurant, open since 2009 on a quiet street in the centre, with modern cooking built on Apulian produce and recipes; listed in the Michelin Guide.
items.name: La Bul
items.note: The Michelin Guide lists other hours (Mon-Sat 19:30-21:30, closed Sunday); the hours above are the restaurant's own. The map point is the street, not the building.

items.description: A gelateria on Corso Cavour going since 1936, also serving granita, filled brioche and coffee, with plenty of fruit and vegan flavours.

image.alt: The street of Gelateria Gasperini dal 1936

items.name: Gelateria Gasperini dal 1936
items.note: No official website found; the 1936 date comes from the shop's name and press listings.

items.description: A small restaurant near Teatro Petruzzelli and the seafront serving Barese and Mediterranean dishes, seafood and spaghetti all'assassina among them.
items.name: Le 2 Aquile
items.note: No guide or press review found; its own page and the listing sites agree on the address.

items.address: Via Vito Nicola De Nicolò 40, 70121 Bari
items.description: A Murat restaurant going for more than fifty years, serving Apulian dishes and fresh fish, and credited as the birthplace of spaghetti all'assassina.

image.alt: A dish Al Sorso Preferito is known for

items.name: Al Sorso Preferito
items.note: Sometimes written "Il Sorso Preferito". Accounts of how the dish was invented differ.

items.description: A bistro opened in 2020 with an open kitchen and outdoor tables, starting from Apulian cured meats, cheeses and tarallini and going on to pasta, fish and meat.

image.alt: The street of Tuccio Cucina e Caffè

items.name: Tuccio Cucina e Caffè
items.note: italia.it gives no. 15, Gambero Rosso no. 13; neither is mapped, so the pin is on the square's odd-numbered side.

items.description: A small restaurant and art space opened in 2019 by gallerist Michele Spinelli and chef Nicola Ricci, pairing Apulian ingredients with Japanese technique among artworks on show.
items.name: Vettor
items.note: The FAQ on the home page gives slightly different hours from the contact page, used above.
items.price: Tasting menus 75 EUR (A mano libera, four seafood courses and a dessert) and 70 EUR (In viaggio).

items.description: A Bari Vecchia alley where local women make and sell fresh orecchiette at their doors, best seen in the morning.
items.iswcTip: The organisers' favourite alley: after the Arco Basso arch, Via delle Orecchiette, with washing hung out, tables of fresh pasta and ladies making it as they chat.
items.name: Strada Arco Basso (orecchiette street)

items.description: A small, plain, centuries-old osteria nicknamed "Il Buco", known for handmade orecchiette (with turnip tops or horse-meat braciola) and tiella of rice, potatoes and mussels.

image.alt: The street of Osteria delle Travi (Il Buco)

items.name: Osteria delle Travi (Il Buco)
items.note: Also listed as "Osteria Le Travi". Sources give 1813 or 1831 as its founding year. No official website found, so check opening times locally.

items.description: A seafood restaurant at the edge of the old town known for raw seafood (crudo, tartare, sea urchins), with seasonal tasting menus and natural and biodynamic wines.
items.name: Biancofiore
items.note: The site's contact page gives other hours (daily 12:00-15:00 and 19:00-23:30) than its footer, used above. Next door to Mastrociccio.
items.price: Tasting menus 60 EUR (six courses, sea or land; wine not included; whole table, minimum 2).

items.description: A panzerotti spot on Corso Vittorio Emanuele II at the edge of the old town.

image.alt: A dish Mastrociccio is known for

items.name: Mastrociccio

items.description: A family-run seafood trattoria in the old town, open since 2014, known for octopus, its roast-octopus sandwich above all, and fried and grilled fish.

image.alt: A dish La Tana del Polpo is known for

items.name: La Tana del Polpo
items.note: No reservations, says its site. The family also runs a street-food counter at Strada Vallisa 41/42 and a second dining room at Via Roberto il Guiscardo 36.

items.description: A bakery going since 1921, known for tomato-and-olive focaccia and panzerotti, with queues mid-morning and around 5 pm.

image.alt: A dish Panificio Santa Rita is known for

items.name: Panificio Santa Rita

items.address: Piazza Federico II di Svevia 33-36, 70122 Bari
items.description: A family gelateria by the Swabian Castle that goes back to a granita kiosk of 1880, known for almond and fiordilatte creams, seasonal fruit and lactose-free flavours.

image.alt: The street of Antica Gelateria Gentile

items.name: Antica Gelateria Gentile
items.note: The official site gives 33-36; Gambero Rosso, BariToday and ConGelato give no. 33.

items.address: Molo San Nicola, next to Teatro Margherita, Bari
items.description: Fishermen selling sea urchins, curled octopus and other raw seafood from their boats and tables on the Molo San Nicola, to eat on the spot.

image.alt: A dish N'derr a la lanze (raw seafood on the pier) is known for

items.name: N'derr a la lanze (raw seafood on the pier)
items.note: Mornings; bring small cash. Sources are food blogs, not an official page.

items.address: Piazza Federico II di Svevia 6/7, 70122 Bari
items.description: A long-established seafood restaurant facing the Swabian Castle, with a fresh-fish counter on display, vaulted rooms and a veranda.
items.name: Al Pescatore
items.note: The restaurant gives no. 6/7; Gambero Rosso says 6 and il Tacco di Bacco 6/8.

items.description: Slices of fried polenta, salted and served hot, sold informally by old-town residents, mostly in the evening.

image.alt: A dish Sgagliozze in Bari Vecchia is known for

items.name: Sgagliozze in Bari Vecchia
items.note: Do Eat Better and Budget Traveller give the best-known spot, Maria delle Sgagliozze's, as Strada delle Crociate 13 (evenings); Fathom puts her at the Arco di San Nicola. Budget Traveller (2026) says her family and other vendors carry on there. The point is the old town, not a shop.

items.description: A historic old-town bakery near the Basilica known for focaccia barese and panzerotti.

image.alt: A dish Panificio Fiore is known for

items.name: Panificio Fiore

items.description: A town just west of Bari with a Romanesque cathedral.
items.iswcTip: Home to Puglia's first national gallery and the region's largest diocesan museum; its cathedral is a key example of Apulian Romanesque, and the town was recognised as a city of art in 2004.
items.name: Bitonto
items.note: Suggested by the organisers; this guide has no checked train details for it.

items.description: A town on the edge of the Alta Murgia with a Romanesque cathedral and an archaeological museum.
items.iswcTip: A city of art in the Alta Murgia National Park, with the Jatta National Archaeological Museum (Hellenistic finds, including the Talos vase); known for its Holy Week.
items.name: Ruvo di Puglia
items.note: Suggested by the organisers; this guide has no checked train details for it.

items.description: A coastal town south-east of Bari, a short hop on the Trenitalia regional line towards Lecce.
items.iswcTip: Suggested by the organisers: Domenico Modugno's hometown on a spur over the sea, with sea caves, white houses on the cliff and terraces with views.
items.journey: About 30 min by regional train (from a Trenitalia service notice, July 2026).
items.name: Polignano a Mare

items.description: A coastal town a few stops past Polignano on the same regional line.

credit.author: Hagai Agmon-Snir حچاي اچمون-سنير חגי אגמון-שניר

items.iswcTip: One of the towns south of Bari the organisers suggest visiting.
items.journey: About 35 min by regional train (from a Trenitalia service notice, July 2026).
items.name: Monopoli

items.address: Trani railway station, Piazza XX Settembre
items.description: A coastal town north-west of Bari on the Adriatic line towards Foggia.
items.iswcTip: Suggested by the organisers as a city of art, with its cathedral on the sea and its Swabian castle.
items.journey: About 1 h on a stopping regional train (from a Trenitalia service notice, August 2026); faster trains may exist.
items.name: Trani

items.description: The town of the conical trulli houses, on the FSE line from Bari towards Martina Franca.
items.iswcTip: Suggested by the organisers: the UNESCO town of trulli; the Rione Monti district has over 1,000 of them, Aia Piccola about 400 more.
items.name: Alberobello
items.note: Journey time not confirmed (the FSE timetable page did not load); the town's site says a change at Putignano may be needed. Check fssudest.it before going.

items.address: Strada Provinciale 8 di Castel del Monte, Andria
items.description: An octagonal hilltop castle near Andria, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.iswcTip: A perfectly octagonal castle, outer walls and courtyard both eight-sided, each side about 10 metres long, mixing Northern European, Islamic and classical elements; on the UNESCO list since 1996.
items.name: Castel del Monte
items.note: Suggested by the organisers; this guide has no checked transport details for it.

items.address: Matera Centrale station, Viale Aldo Moro
items.description: The town of the Sassi cave districts in Basilicata, reached on the narrow-gauge FAL line from its own platform at Bari Centrale.
items.journey: About 1 h 45 min, usually changing at Altamura (worked out from the FAL timetable valid from 12 Oct 2026); on Sundays and holidays FAL runs replacement buses.
items.name: Matera

items.description: A white hill town of the Itria Valley with a round historic centre.
items.iswcTip: One of Italy's most beautiful villages, its name meaning 'round place' after the circular town plan, known for its cummerse: houses with sloping roofs of limestone slabs called chiancarelle.
items.name: Locorotondo
items.note: Suggested by the organisers; this guide has no checked train details for it.

items.description: The whitewashed hill town of the Brindisi province, between olive groves and the sea.
items.iswcTip: The 'White City', its houses whitewashed with quicklime; La Terra, the historic centre, is a tangle of alleys, squares and stairways crowned by a sixteenth-century cathedral.
items.name: Ostuni
items.note: Suggested by the organisers; this guide has no checked train details for it.

practical.text: The organisers suggest the cathedral, the Basilica of Saint Nicholas, the Swabian Castle, the old town (Bari Vecchia, between the old and new ports) and the underground remains of the old city, the Nazario Sauro seafront and the shopping streets around Via Sparano. Nearby towns they name: Polignano, Monopoli, Alberobello, Locorotondo and Cisternino to the south; Giovinazzo, Trani, Altamura and Castel del Monte to the north. The Sights and Day trips tabs mark their suggestions.
practical.title: What to see

practical.text: The organising secretariat is CIC Sud (Centro Italiano Congressi Bari), iswc2026@cicsud.it. Visa invitation letters are only issued to registered participants (subject "Visa Request – ISWC 2026"); cancellations and changes go to the same address in writing.
practical.title: Conference secretariat

practical.text: Childcare is not a service offered by the conference. The site lists independent providers of babysitting in English; contact them directly about availability, rates and bookings. The secretariat (iswc2026@cicsud.it) offers further help.
practical.title: Childcare

practical.text: To report any behaviour that makes you or others uncomfortable, contact any of the SWSA members, by email or in person; they treat reports confidentially.
practical.title: Code of conduct
